title: build(deps): bump python dependencies
author: Red-GV
body:
# Changes

This is a more manual intervention for #2232 , which cannot update due to some issue described within that PR.

## Merge Requirements

For new features contributions, please make sure you have completed the following
essential items:

* [ ] `CHANGELOG.md` updated to document new feature additions
* [ ] Appropriate documentation updates in the [docs][]
* [ ] Appropriate Helm chart updates in the [helm-charts][]

<!--
A Pull Request that modifies instrumentation code will likely require an
update in docs. Please make sure to update the opentelemetry.io repo with any
docs changes.

A Pull Request that modifies docker-compose.yaml, otelcol-config.yaml, or
Grafana dashboards will likely require an update to the Demo Helm chart.
Other changes affecting how a service is deployed will also likely require an
update to the Demo Helm chart.
-->

Maintainers will not merge until the above have been completed. If you're unsure
which docs need to be changed ping the
[@open-telemetry/demo-approvers](https://github.com/orgs/open-telemetry/teams/demo-approvers).

[docs]: https://opentelemetry.io/docs/demo/
[helm-charts]: https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-helm-charts

comments.author: julianocosta89
comments.text: @Red-GV there are some conflicts on the dependencies, would you be able to take a look in the failing checks?

comments.author: Red-GV
comments.text: Yeah, I'm doing that now. I probably should've put this into draft mode first.

comments.author: Red-GV
comments.text: Oh @julianocosta89 , would you prefer the `requirements.txt` to be the full print out of `pip freeze` or just the required modules which will install everything?

comments.author: julianocosta89
comments.text:
> Oh @julianocosta89 , would you prefer the `requirements.txt` to be the full print out of `pip freeze` or just the required modules which will install everything?

@Red-GV what is the best practice on that?

comments.author: Red-GV
comments.text: I'm not entirely sure myself. I've seen some guidance that it should only be the packages needed, but others may disagree because you won't catch on to dependencies of those packages which have vulnerabilities. Though upgrading those dependencies can be a bit tricky if the main package hasn't updated them. At one point in my own projects, I had tried to use a `requirements-freeze.txt` file to try and do the best of both worlds, but I had dropped it later down the track.
